pr.title: Add horizontal resize support for quick input widget
pr.body:
## Summary

- Adds draggable resize handles on the left and right edges of the quick input widget, allowing users to horizontally resize the command palette / quick pick
- The widget stays centered while resizing — both edges expand/contract symmetrically
- The custom width is persisted in application storage and restored across sessions

Fixes #85374


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3275288a-8952-43fd-8937-d847b29b8345




## Test plan

- [x] Open the command palette (`Cmd+P` or `Cmd+Shift+P`) and verify resize handles appear on the left and right edges
- [x] Drag the right edge to widen/narrow the widget — it should stay centered
- [x] Drag the left edge to widen/narrow the widget — it should stay centered
- [x] Close and reopen the command palette — the custom width should be restored
- [x] Resize after dragging the widget to a custom position — verify it stays centered at that position
- [x] Verify the widget respects minimum width (300px) and maximum width (900px / container bounds)

reviews.body:
## Pull request overview

Adds horizontal resize support to the quick input widget (command palette / quick pick), including persistence of custom width via stored view state.

**Changes:**
- Persist and restore a custom quick input width via `workbench.quickInput.viewState`.
- Add a `QuickInputResizeController` that provides left/right resize handles, drag resizing, and double-click reset.
- Add CSS for the resize handle hit targets.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `src/vs/platform/quickinput/browser/quickInputController.ts` | Introduces persisted `width` in view state, adds resize controller + layout updates, and implements mouse-driven resize behavior. |
| `src/vs/platform/quickinput/browser/media/quickInput.css` | Styles/positions the new resize handle elements on the widget edges. |

comments.body:
Any chance of progress in the upcoming releases? This PR would solve this already 7 year old issue https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/85374#issuecomment-3939690996 ....
What can be done to help with this?

@TylerLeonhardt 👋
Sorry for tagging directly, but community would appreciate a lot if you could invest some of your time and look at this PR. Thanks! 🙏

Hi, I have used OpenAI Codex to implement a resizable Quick Input. I have tested it in various scenarios including multiple VS Code instances and persistence and couldn't find any issue. Please let me know if I should open a PR or if you want to integrate some of the code in yours.

The code is available in [my fork](https://github.com/wilhem-meignan/vscode/tree/quick-input-resize-85374).

Here is a short description of the work:

> User-facing behavior: Quick-input widgets can be resized symmetrically from the left or right edge and vertically from the bottom edge or either bottom corner. Width and height are constrained to the available window and content, persisted between sessions, and restored safely when the window becomes smaller. Filtered lists cannot be enlarged beyond their visible content, while the preferred height is retained when the filter is cleared. Double-clicking the header resets size and position.
> Implementation: It uses VS Code’s native Sash component for handles, corner interaction, and directional cursors. Resize events update the existing persisted quick-input view state, and layout calculations clamp the resulting size and position. Content-height events trigger recalculation when filtering changes the list.
> Anchored quick-input widgets are explicitly excluded: their resize sashes are disabled so their existing anchor-based layout remains unaffected. The implementation includes browser tests covering edges, corners, constraints, filtering, persistence, restoration, reset, and anchored widgets.

Note that the vertical resizing happens one line at a time and there is a few pixels of the next line visible on purpose so that the user can see when more lines are available.

commit.message:
Add horizontal resize support for quick input widget

Allow users to resize the command palette / quick input widget by
dragging its left or right edge. The custom width is persisted in
storage and restored across sessions. Double-clicking a resize handle
resets the width to the default.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#85374

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Keep quick input centered while resizing

Remove edge-anchoring behavior so the widget stays centered during
resize. Also remove the double-click-to-reset-width feature.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
